MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  May 11, 2021
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at
5:01 p.m., on May 11, 2021, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on May 6, 2021, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at the
Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Member Bucknum
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Labor Negotiations - The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957 and 54957.6. The Parties to the
  Negotiations Are the City and City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s Negotiator
  is Dennis Wilberg.

CS2. Conference with Real Property Negotiators: Stein Mart Property 25282 Marguerite
  Parkway; Agency Negotiators: Dennis Wilberg, Keith Rattay, Elaine Lister, Cheryl
  Dyas and William Curley. Negotiating Party: Kinstler Family Trust. Under Negotiation-
  Price and Terms

City Council Minutes  1  May 11, 2021
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:02 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there were two Closed Session Items this evening. The
City Council was updated and gave staff direction, but no reportable action occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Raths

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Winner of the Mission Viejo Library Comic Fest 2021 Art Showcase

  Recognized Vincent Dokken.

P2. School Spotlight - Trabuco Hills High School

  Receive presentation Kara Johnson Special Education Teacher and UCS District Liaison and
  Principal Alicia Foulk.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Goodell, Bucknum, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of April 27, 2021, as presented.

2.  Check Register Dated April 16, 2021 in the Amount of $602,092.81

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register dated April 23, 2021 in the amount of $811,701.38

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

City Council Minutes  2  May 11, 2021
 4.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for March 2021

  Received and filed.

5.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for March 2021

  Received and filed.

6.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report
  for March 2021

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for March 2021

  Received and filed.

8.  Transmittal of Pre-PARE Trustee Reports for the quarter ending March 31, 2021

  Received and filed the accompanying Pre-PARE Trustee Reports for the Quarter ending
  March 31, 2021.

9.  2021-2023 School Crossing Guard Services

  Approved the Second Amendment to with American Guard Services, Inc., to modify certain
  terms of the contract contingent upon approval of the Fiscal Year 2021-2023 budget.

10. Barcelona Walls - Intersections of Alicia Parkway and Muirlands Blvd. and Alicia
  Parkway and Charlinda Drive- (CIP 21330)

  (1) Awarded a contract to SDC Engineering, Inc. for the construction of a Barcelona Wall at
  the intersection of Alicia Parkway and Charlinda Drive. in an amount not to exceed
  $69,750.00, and (2) adopted Resolution 21-10 Adjustment of Costs Relating to (CIP 21330).

11. City of Mission Viejo Renewed Measure M (M2) Eligibility: MPAH Consistency and
  Mitigation Fee Program Components

  Adopt Resolution 21-11 Concerning the Status and Update of the General Plan Circulation
  Element and Mitigation Fee Program for the Renewed Measure M (M2) Program, and direct
  staff to transmit said resolution to the Orange County Transportation Authority by June 30,
  2021, to maintain the City's continued eligibility in receiving FY2021/22 M2 local fair share
  revenues and in pursuing competitive grant funding opportunities.

City Council Minutes  3  May 11, 2021
 12. Draft 2021-2022 Annual Action Plan Detailing the Proposed Use of Community
  Development Block Grant (CDBG) Funds

  Adopted Resolution 21-12 Approving the City's 2021-2022 Annual Action Plan Detailing the
  Proposed Use of Community Development Block Grant Funds, and Authorizing Submission
  of the Plan to the United States Department of Housing and Urban Development.

13. Amendment to Agreement for Building Plan Check and Inspection Services - Charles
  Abbott Associates, Inc.

  Approved the First Amendment to Agreement with Charles Abbott Associates, Inc. for
  Building Plan Check and Inspection Services for the Period from July 1, 2021 to June 30,
  2023.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

OLD BUSINESS

14. Establish General Fund Target and Minimum Reserve Levels for 2021-23 Budget Cycle

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to adopt
  Resolution 21-13 Establishing General Fund Target and Minimum Reserve Levels for the
  2021-23 Budget Cycle.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Goodell, Bucknum, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

15. FY 2021-2023 Proposed CIP Budget

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Council Member Sachs asked if there are recommendations for the half a million in lieu of
  shade structures at parks. Director Dyas said they did not.

  Council Member Sachs asked if Council would entertain the foregoing of half a million dollars
  for shade structures until staff has had a better opportunity to look at potential other uses? He
  indicated that he is not against shade structures but that if there are other things of priority
  should we not be looking at that.

  Mayor Kelley stated that the parks are extremely hot during the summer and the trees are not
  full grown to provide the shade needed for the playground equipment.

  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum said she would like to see all the other options.
City Council Minutes  4  May 11, 2021
   Council Member Goodell recalled the discussions of deferring the shade structures until the
  rehab of the parks so that it could go together in the design of the parks. He stated he is in
  favor of continuing with the plan set out two years ago.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum to approve
  the item with the exception of half a million dollars for further review to the agenda item.

  Mayor Kelley opposed the motion.

  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum asked staff if the shade structure cost included in the Coronado
  Park Renovation? City Manager Dennis Wilberg said yes. She stated she is supportive of the
  shade structure at Coronado Park and would like to revisit this going forward for the other
  parks. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum removed her second on Council Member Sachs’ motion.

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to move
  the staff’s recommendation and that direction for additional discussion of alternatives be held
  at a future meeting and that progress of the two parks being currently renovated continue.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Goodell, Bucknum, Kelley, and Raths
  NOES:  Sachs
  ABSENT:  None

PUBLIC HEARINGS

16. Ordinance to Allow and Regulate Residential Beekeeping in the City of Mission Viejo

  Staff report was presented by Director of Community Development Elaine Lister and
  Planning and Economic Development Manager Larry Longenecker.

  Mayor Kelley opened the Public Hearing at 7:12 p.m.

  The following spoke in favor of the Beekeeping Ordinance: Maya Cappellino, Ladera Ranch;
  Avram Grossman, Irvine; Ron Vanderhoff, Lake Forest; Teresa Karr, Laguna Niguel; Liz
  Savage, Fullerton; and Kristy, M.V.

  The following spoke in opposition of the Beekeeping Ordinance: David Allen, M.V.; Ray
  Imatani, M.V.; and Jerry Bryant, M.V.

  Written comments were received in favor of the Beekeeping Ordinance: Meredith Rushing;
  Meg Upton, M.V.; Megan Fix, M.V.; Tom Sandefur; Philippe Tusler; Briana Jokerst, M.V.;
  Colleen Eberhardt; Brittney Holbrook, M.V.; Martin Brix; Sam Lai, M.V.; Milan Rousset;
  Carla St. Laurent, MD, M.V.; Haley Barragan; Barbara Hosmer, M.V.; Jon & Mami Humann,
  M.V.; Kristin Delcamp, M.V.; Linda Cooper; Stacie Aguesse, M.V.; Michael Buhrley, M.V.;
  Louise Karkoutli, M.V.; and Tim Montano, M.V.

City Council Minutes  5  May 11, 2021
   Written comments were received in opposition of the Beekeeping Ordinance: Alexis
  Jacovides, M.V.; Karen Lee, M.V.; Ranbir and Ranjana Wasu, M.V.; Sue Nelson, M.V.;
  Vickee Donoho, M.V.; Edith Schmitt, M.V.; Cathy Allen, M.V.; Diane Norton, M.V.; Charles
  and Sandy Allen, M.V.; Robbi Doncost, M.V.; Dawn Turner, M.V.; Lauren Ramey, M.V.;
  Beth Dickinson, M.V.; Ali Salem, M.V.; Ashley Johnson; Adi Mitchell; Bryn DenHeyer,
  M.V.; Robert Goldstein, M.V.; Ansley Burke, M.V.; Tracey Riness, M.V.; David Allen,
  M.V.; Clayton Riness, M.V.; Jaye Salvin, M.V.; Graham Mather, M.V.; Donna and Ken
  White, M.V.; Nancy Wilson, M.V.; Anthony and Joanne Scarabino, M.V.; Susan Mruskovic;
  Sharon Ames, M.V.; Alison Sward, M.V.; Randy Smith, M.V.; Pam Smith, M.V.; Robert
  Elam, M.V.; Brenda Cooper, M.V.; Hugh Feeney, M.V.; Kathy and Ed Dittner, M.V.; Cathy
  Baranger, M.V.; Jeanne Feeney, M.V.; Susan Fouts, M.V.; and Art Levine, M.V.

  Mayor Kelley closed the Public Hearing at 7:44 p.m.

  Council Members asked various questions regarding beekeeping.

  Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell to deny the
  introduction of an Ordinance Amending Section 10.01.010 and Adding Article 9 of Chapter
  10.01 of the Mission Viejo Municipal Code Regarding Regulations for Residential
  Beekeeping.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Raths
  NOES:  Sachs
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

17. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) Report

  Received report from Council Member Goodell.

  Mayor Kelley asked that an OCTA Representative come to a future Council Meeting and
  give an update on timelines of their various projects.

CITY MANAGER REPORT

18. Community Choice Aggregation Update

  Received report from Management Analyst Susan Patterson.

19. Lower Curtis Park Update Report

  Received report from Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

City Council Minutes  6  May 11, 2021
 20. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell had no additional comments this evening.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths stated that he does not appreciate people from other communities addressing
the Council that we need to put bee hives in our backyards. He asked the City Manager if we could
have Cox Cable come to a future meeting and make a presentation on cable and internet services.
Council Member Raths said it was good to be back and the City looks great. He mentioned a new
grocery store going up on Crown Valley and he appreciates all the hard work the past year from
staff and police services.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs voiced concerns of people continuing to run red lights through out the City.
He asked questions of Lieutenant Vuong questions. Lieutenant Vuong addressed his questions and
stated that it has been a trend throughout Orange County, not just in Mission Viejo. Council
Member Sachs thanked the Sheriff’s department for all that they do.

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum mentioned that Council Member Sachs raises butterflies and suggested
that residents raise butterflies. She wished all he mom’s a Happy Mother’s Day and mentioned that
her son took her to Oso Creek Golf Course for lunch and the food was fabulous. She encourages
residents to check it out. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum announced that there will be a food drive at the
Norman P, Murray Center this weekend benefiting South County Outreach. On May 22, there will
be a drive through Water Safety Challenge at the Marguerite Aquatics Center from 9:00 – 11:00
a.m. Lastly, she announced that in the civic center parking lot there is an American Heroes Tribute
set up and there will be a virtual Memorial Day Ceremony and drive through between 8:30 and
10:30 a.m., however residents can come and see the display now.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley thanked Council Member Sachs for bringing up the red-light running issue and she
encouraged everyone to wait a few seconds when the light turns green before proceeding through
the intersections. She announced that there is a good recycling center in Mission Viejo called Next
Generation Recycling and it is on Centre Drive by the Animal Shelter in the side parking lot of the
Crown Valley Market. She stated that they are open from 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. Lastly, she thanked
the Explorers this evening for escorting people into the Council Chamber.

City Council Minutes  7  May 11, 2021
 ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:06 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting to Tuesday May 25, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of May 25, 2021

City Council Minutes  8  May 11, 2021
